report:
**Conclusion**  
Your assessment is correct: available scientific evidence does not support the claim that taking ibuprofen worsens a COVID-19 infection.

**Evidence Summary**
* **Anecdotal Origins:** Concerns regarding ibuprofen originated early in the pandemic (March 2020) due to unconfirmed anecdotal reports and theoretical assumptions rather than robust clinical research (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7287029/).
* **Lack of Evidence for Harm:** Health agencies, including the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and European Medicines Agency (EMA), examined reported concerns and found no scientific evidence connecting non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) use to worsening COVID-19 outcomes (https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-alerts-and-statements/fda-advises-patients-use-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs-nsaids-covid-19; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7537121/).
* **Official Guidance:** Following extensive reviews of observational data, major international health bodies—including the World Health Organization (WHO), EMA, and FDA—decided against recommending the avoidance of ibuprofen or other NSAIDs for managing COVID-19 symptoms (https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lanrhe/article/PIIS2665-9913(21)00144-2/fulltext).
